name: Waldorf Versailles Trianon Palace
positioning: Historic hotel at the edge of the Chateau de Versailles gardens, on its site since 1910; officially Waldorf Astoria Versailles - Trianon Palace
best_for: Travelers who want to walk straight into the Chateau de Versailles gardens
History lovers drawn to the ballroom linked to the Treaty of Versailles
Families who want a kids club

facts.text: The hotel sits at the edge of the Chateau de Versailles gardens and has occupied its site since 1910.
The architecture takes its inspiration from the Grand Trianon at Versailles.
The Trianon Palace building features neoclassical architecture and a grand gallery filled with daylight.
The hotel has two sections, Trianon Palace and Pavillon du Trianon.
Most Pavillon du Trianon rooms overlook the hotel's gardens.
Palace suites have a separate living area and views of the Chateau and its Royal Domain.
Rooms have mosaic-tiled marble bathrooms with heated floors.
La Véranda brasserie serves breakfast, lunch and dinner with continental cuisine.
Peacock Alley serves afternoon tea and a wide selection of wines.
The hotel's culinary duo is Executive Chef Frédéric Larquemin and Pastry Chef Eddie Benghanem.
There is a kids club for younger guests.
The hotel has a conference center for corporate meetings and events.

highlights.text: The Salon Clemenceau, the hotel's historic ballroom, hosted the official delegations working out the details of the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.
Guests can walk directly from the hotel into the Chateau de Versailles gardens.
The architect, René Sergent, also designed the Savoy and Claridge's hotels in London.
The Guerlain spa's treatment rooms are arranged around a glass-roofed swimming pool.
In warmer months, La Véranda's terrace has a view of the Palace of Versailles.

considerations.text: The restaurants, bar, spa and swimming pool are all in the Palace building; Pavillon du Trianon guests reach them by a dedicated pathway.
Condé Nast Traveler advises requesting a garden- or park-facing room in the historic hotel rather than the newer annex.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is outside central Paris, so city sights need transportation.
